scores.name: Human before agenda
scores.description: Did the meeting open with the person rather than the portfolio? (Kinder / Mitch Anthony; Somers)

anchors.low: Numbers within the first minute, no check-in.
anchors.high: Genuine opening conversation, and the client shaped the agenda.

criteria.text: The adviser opened by asking how the client is doing, and engaged with the answer rather than treating it as a formality.
Life events mentioned by the client were acknowledged before moving to financials.
The client was asked what would make the meeting most useful to them, and the agenda reflected the answer.

scores.name: Listening share
scores.description: Anchored to the deterministic metrics; reflections as well as questions. (MI/OARS)

anchors.low: Adviser talk share 65% or more, or a monologue over 4 minutes.
anchors.high: Share 45% or below, with reflections and follow-ups that build on the client's own words.

criteria.text: Per the computed metrics, the adviser spoke less than the client (or close to parity).
The adviser's questions built on what the client had just said, rather than returning to a script.
The adviser used reflective listening - restating the client's meaning or feeling before responding - not only questions.
Long explanations were broken with checks rather than delivered as monologues.

scores.name: Behavioural coaching moments
scores.description: Naming anxiety before answering it, and rehearsing turbulence before it arrives. (Murray; Vanguard; Davies; Voss/NURSE)

anchors.low: Client anxiety met with a prediction or brushed past; no forward-looking coaching.
anchors.high: Anxiety named before it was answered AND future turbulence rehearsed unprompted.

criteria.text: When the client expressed worry, the adviser named the concern before answering it.
Reassurance was anchored to the client's plan and long-term evidence, not to predictions about markets, tax, or politics.
The adviser separated what is controllable from what is not, out loud.
Proactive inoculation: at some point the adviser rehearsed a future bad patch before it exists, rather than only reacting to raised fears.

anchors.high: Every technical term translated at first use, and understanding tested by invitation, not assumption.

criteria.text: Technical terms were either avoided or explained in ordinary words at first use.
Understanding was checked by inviting the client to say it back in their own words - teach-back, not just "does that make sense?".

scores.name: Agreements & adherence
scores.description: Adherence is designed, not hoped for. (Somers; shared decision-making)

anchors.high: Readback confirmed aloud, action load kept small, first step easy, obstacles anticipated.

criteria.text: Every decision reached was restated by the adviser in one sentence, and the client audibly confirmed each.
Next steps were assigned out loud - what the adviser does, what the client does, and roughly by when.
The client's action load was kept deliberately small (roughly three items or fewer), with the first step easy and near-term.
Likely obstacles to follow-through were asked about or anticipated ("what would get in the way of this?").

scores.name: Anchored to their why
scores.description: Recommendations tied to what this client said they want. (Kinder; Mitch Anthony; Statman; Davies)

anchors.low: Recommendations justified only by product or tax logic.
anchors.high: Each material recommendation explicitly tied back to something this client said they want.

criteria.text: Recommendations were linked out loud to the client's own stated goals, values, or life plans ("because you said you want X..."), not only to returns, tax, or product features.
The client's own words for what matters were used, not the adviser's substitutes.
Where a goal had shifted, the shift was surfaced before advice was given on it.

scores.name: Both voices
scores.description: Couples meetings only. Single-client meetings are not_assessable by definition.

anchors.low: One client near-silent and never drawn in.
anchors.mid: Both spoke, but one clearly carried it.
anchors.high: Shares within roughly 2:1, quieter partner directly invited, and each confirmed decisions individually.

criteria.text: Per the computed metrics, speaking time between the two clients was reasonably balanced (worse than ~3:1 should pull down; better than ~2:1 supports a high score).
The quieter partner was directly invited in by name at least twice, including on at least one substantive decision.
Goals questions were put to each partner individually, not only to the couple jointly.
Each decision was confirmed aloud by both, not by one on behalf of two.
